title: Gurbakhsh Singh Rejects Heaven and Charges the Enemy

blocks.text: Here the page gathers the inner meaning of the vow into a concise declaration. Company of the Khalsa is what they craved for, not the rewards of paradise, so martyrdom is presented as fidelity to the Panth rather than as a private search for heavenly compensation.

That conviction immediately translates into conduct under fire. Not a single Singh turned his back from the fight, even as many a shot did they fire on Singhs from their muskets and the pressure of the Gilja attack grew heavier around Gurbakhsh Singh's small band.

Gurbakhsh Singh responds by moving from exhortation to direct action. Gurbakhsh Singh threw away his own shield so that he could strike more freely, showing that he seeks a face-to-face death in combat and not merely survival beneath defensive cover.
